findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: account_status, profiles_manage, posts_manage, inbox_messages, comments_moderate, ads_campaigns, blogs_publish · Private data: account_register, account_status, profiles_manage, accounts_manage, posts_manage, media_pipeline, telecom_numbers · Public sink: account_register, billing_upgrade, posts_publish, media_pipeline, comments_moderate, ads_campaigns, blogs_publish, telecom_numbers, telecom_messaging · Destructive: profiles_manage, accounts_manage, posts_manage, media_pipeline, comments_moderate, analytics_query.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: account_status, profiles_manage, posts_manage, inbox_messages, comments_moderate, ads_campaigns, blogs_publish · Private data: account_register, account_status, profiles_manage, accounts_manage, posts_manage, media_pipeline, telecom_numbers · Public sink: account_register, billing_upgrade, posts_publish, media_pipeline, comments_moderate, ads_campaigns, blogs_publish, telecom_numbers, telecom_messaging · Destructive: profiles_manage, accounts_manage, posts_manage, media_pipeline, comments_moderate, analytics_query

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
